what.text: A state machine diagram shows the states of one thing, and the events that move it between them.

water.text: Water can be liquid, vapor, or ice. Freezing moves it from liquid to ice. Condensation, from vapor to liquid.

off.text: Now an A T M. It starts Off. The black dot is the initial pseudostate.

on.text: Power on. It runs its startup and enters Self Test.

fail.text: If the test fails: Out of Service. Otherwise, with no trigger at all, it moves to Idle.

card.text: A customer inserts a card. The A T M moves to Serving Customer, and on entry, it reads the card.

composite.text: Serving Customer is a composite state. Inside are three substates in sequence: authentication, selecting a transaction, and the transaction.

cancel.text: The customer can cancel at any time. That goes straight back to Idle.

exit.text: And whatever the reason for leaving, the exit action ejects the card.

kinds.text: A simple state has no substates. A composite state has substates. And a shallow history state returns to the last substate that was active.
